title: Flat apple & vanilla tart
keywords: apple, tart, vanilla, baking, puff pastry
ingredients: 5 large eating apples - Cox's, russets or Elstar
3 tsp vanilla sugar or 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Heat oven to 220C/fan 200C/gas 7. Roll out the pastry and trim to a round about 35cm across. Transfer to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Peel, core and thinly slice the apples and toss in the lemon juice. Spread over the pastry to within 2cm of the edges. Curl up the edges slightly to stop the juices running off.
Dot the top with the butter and sprinkle with vanilla and caster sugar. Bake for 15-20 mins until the apples are tender and the pastry crisp.
Warm the conserve and brush over the apples and pastry edge. Serve hot with vanilla ice cream or crème fraîche.
notes: Serve hot with vanilla ice cream or crème fraîche.

title: Fluffy American pancakes
ingredients: 2 tbsp melted butter (allowed to cool slightly) or olive oil, plus extra for cooking
instructions: Sift the flour, baking powder, salt and caster sugar into a large bowl. In a separate bowl or jug, lightly whisk together the milk and egg, then whisk in the melted butter.
Pour the milk mixture into the flour mixture and, using a fork, beat until you have a smooth batter. Any lumps will soon disappear with a little mixing. Let the batter stand for a few minutes.

Heat a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat and add a knob of butter. When it's melted, add a ladle of batter (or two if your frying pan is big enough to cook two pancakes at the same time). It will seem very thick but this is how it should be. Wait until the top of the pancake begins to bubble, then turn it over and cook until both sides are golden brown and the pancake has risen to about 1 cm / 1/2 in thick.
Repeat until all the batter is used up. You can keep the pancakes warm in a low oven, but they taste best fresh out the pan.
Serve with lashings of real maple syrup and extra butter, if you like.
notes: For extra-fluffy pancakes substitute self-raising flour for plain flour and still use the baking powder.

title: Scotch Eggs
keywords: scotch eggs, black pudding, chorizo, pork, eggs, deep fry
ingredients: Medium eggs, at room temperature (6 for filling, 1-2 for coating)
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Bring a pan of water to the boil, add the 6 eggs and cook for 6 minutes for a soft-set yolk. Drain, run under cold water, and carefully shell them.
Set out three coating bowls: flour seasoned with salt and pepper, beaten egg, and coarse breadcrumbs.
Prepare your chosen meat mixture (see variants), flatten into 6cm discs, enclose a boiled egg, seal joins well, and coat in flour, egg, and breadcrumbs. Chill until ready to cook.
Heat oil to 175°C, fry 2-3 eggs at a time for 2 minutes until golden, then transfer to the oven for 10 minutes. Drain and rest for 5-10 minutes.

title: Thai Red Curry
keywords: thai, red curry, coconut milk, curry paste, spicy, asian

components.name: Homemade Thai Red Curry Paste
components.description: A fragrant, fresh spice paste that forms the aromatic base of the curry.
ingredients: 2 dried red chillies, soaked in hot water for 10 minutes
3 lemongrass stalks, outer skin removed, finely sliced
6 fresh kaffir lime leaves or finely grated zest of 1 lime
5cm piece fresh galangal or ginger, finely grated
instructions: Toast the cumin and coriander seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, then grind finely.
In a mortar and pestle or food processor, process the aromatics starting with dry spices, then garlic, lemongrass, coriander roots, lime leaves, and galangal.
Finally add the soaked chillies and shrimp paste, pounding or processing into a thick, smooth paste.

components.name: Curry Main Dish
components.description: The main curry assembly with coconut milk, vegetables, and your choice of protein.
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil or groundnut oil
1 tbsp brown sugar or palm sugar
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the red curry paste and fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and oil begins to separate.
Pour in half of the coconut milk and stir well with the curry paste, simmering for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, and sugar. Bring to a gentle boil.
Add the bell pepper and bamboo shoots, then simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in the torn kaffir lime leaves and fresh Thai basil leaves just before removing from heat. Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

variants.name: Chicken
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil or groundnut oil
1 tbsp brown sugar or palm sugar
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the red curry paste and fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and oil begins to separate.
Pour in half of the coconut milk and simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Add the sliced chicken and cook until it starts to turn white on the outside (about 3-4 minutes).
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, and sugar. Bring to a gentle boil.
Add the bell pepper and bamboo shoots, then simmer for 10-15 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the torn kaffir lime leaves and fresh Thai basil leaves just before removing from heat. Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

variants.name: Seafood & Prawn
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil or groundnut oil
1 tbsp brown sugar or palm sugar
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the red curry paste and fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and oil begins to separate.
Pour in half of the coconut milk and simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, fish sauce, and sugar. Bring to a gentle boil.
Add the bell pepper, bamboo shoots, and mixed seafood, then simmer gently for only 5-8 minutes until seafood is just cooked through.
Stir in the torn kaffir lime leaves and fresh Thai basil leaves just before removing from heat. Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

variants.name: Tofu & Vegetarian
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil or groundnut oil
2 tbsp soy sauce (substitute for fish sauce)
1 tbsp brown sugar or palm sugar
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the red curry paste and fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and oil begins to separate.
Pour in half of the coconut milk and simmer for 3-4 minutes.
Add the pan-fried firm tofu cubes to the simmering base.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, soy sauce, and sugar. Bring to a gentle boil.
Add the bell pepper and bamboo shoots, then simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Stir in the torn kaffir lime leaves and fresh Thai basil leaves just before removing from heat. Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

notes: Curry paste can be made up to 1 week in advance and stored in the fridge.
